title: CRLR/165/2012 of SMT. MEERA YADAV Vs STATE THROUGH GOVERMENT OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 165 of 2012
Smt. Meera Yadav .....Revisionist

Versus
State of Uttarakhand and another ......Respondents
None appears for the revisionist.
Mrs. Mamta Joshi, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.
None appears on behalf of the respondent no. 2.
Dated: 01st September, 2019
Hon'ble N.S. Dhanik, J.
 This revision is preferred against the
judgment and order dated 26.07.2012 passed by the
learned Judge, Family Court, Haridwar in Case No.89
of 2009, Smt. Meera Yadav vs. Sanjay Yadav,
whereby the learned Judge, Family Court, Haridwar
allowed the application filed u/s 125 Cr.P.C.
2. Brief facts of the case are that an
application under Section 125 Cr.P.C. was moved by
the revisionist-wife against the respondent no. 2-
husband for granting interim maintenance. The
learned Court below had dismissed the application of
the revisionist under Section 125 Cr.P.C. Aggrieved
thereby, the instant criminal revision has been
preferred.
3. Mrs. Mamta Joshi, learned Brief Holder for
the State submits that there is no illegality in the

2
impugned judgment and the court below has rightly
rejected the application of the revisionist under
Section 125 Cr.P.C. She further placed reliance on
the judgment of this Court in the case of Ganesh
Nagarkoti vs. State of Uttarakhand reported in
2010 (1) NCC 389.
4. From the perusal of the impugned
judgment, it is clear that the application of the
revisionist-wife under Section 125 Cr.P.C. was
dismissed on the ground that husband-respondent
no. 2 is ready to keep his wife and son with him but
the wife-revisionist was not agree with the same and
claimed maintenance.
5. The court below held that the wife
(revisionist herein) is residing separately with the
husband (respondent no.2 herein) without any
appropriate reasons. Husband is ready to keep her
with himself. Respondent no. 2 has also instituted a
suit for the restitution of conjugal rights under
Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act. Yet the
revisionist refused to live with her husband and
claimed maintenance. Therefore, on these grounds
and relying on the judgment of Ganesh Nagarkoti
vs. State of Uttarakhand reported in 2010 (1) NCC
389; the application of the revisionist (wife) filed
under Section 125 Cr.P.C. was rejected by the Court
below.

3
6. None appears for the revisionist. None was
also present on the previous date also. Even on
behalf of the respondent no. 2 none turns up.
7. Having perused the material on record and
impugned judgment, I agree with the findings of the
court below. There is no illegality or irregularity in
the impugned judgment. Accordingly, the revision is
liable to be dismissed.

8. Since the present revision lacks merit,
accordingly, the same is dismissed and the order
dated 26.07.2012 passed by the learned Judge,
Family Court, Haridwar in Case No.89 of 2009, Smt.
Meera Yadav vs. Sanjay Yadav, is hereby affirmed.
9. Let a copy of this judgment and order,
along with the LCR, be sent back.
